title: Segment Anything Models for medical image segmentation: From native capabilities to clinical requirements.
abstract: Medical image segmentation is essential for computer-aided diagnosis and precision medicine, yet conventional supervised models depend heavily on high-quality annotations and often generalize poorly across domains. The Segment Anything Model (SAM) family offers a transferable, interactive, and extensible foundation for segmentation, but direct medical transfer remains limited by domain gaps, insufficient modeling of medical semantics and anatomy, and mismatches in high-dimensional volumetric and sequential imaging scenarios. This review critically examines the evolution and native capability boundaries of SAM, SAM 2, and SAM 3. Across generations, native capabilities expand from spatial prompting to sequential propagation and concept-level target specification, without automatically conferring medical expertise. We organize medical adaptation from three connected perspectives: model adaptation and strategy selection, task knowledge organization and utilization, and application-oriented adaptation. Cross-method analysis shows that no strategy is universally optimal; effectiveness depends on the gap between foundation-model capabilities and target-task requirements, together with data scale, domain discrepancy, imaging dimensionality, computational resources, and clinical constraints. We further identify four priorities for clinical translation: standardized evaluation for cross-study comparability, controlled continual adaptation under clinical domain drift, dynamic resource scheduling for high-dimensional and real-time workflows, and uncertainty stratification and clinical reliability control. Overall, further progress depends on accurate capability assessment, condition-matched adaptation, and explicit control of computational and prediction risks.

title: HybPromptSeg: Spatial-frequency hybrid prompting for unified multi-task medical image segmentation.
abstract: Fully automated segmentation of medical images is essential for streamlining clinical workflows and improving diagnostic efficiency. However, building a single model that jointly handles multiple segmentation tasks remains challenging because different tasks may vary not only in target structures but also in heterogeneous data distributions. Existing learnable-prompt methods encode task-specific priors, but their generalization may still be constrained by cross-task interference when the tasks have substantially different data distributions. In this study, we propose Hybrid Prompt-based Segmentation, referred to as HybPromptSeg, which is a hybrid prompt-driven, encoder-decoder-based network that unifies multiple medical image segmentation tasks within a single shared model. Concretely, we introduce a Unified Hybrid Prompt (UHP) mechanism that integrates spatial-domain and Fourier-amplitude representations within a shared learnable prompt to model task- and modality-related variations. We further design a Task-conditioned Prompt Generation (TPG) module that generates discriminative task-conditioned prompts to guide the decoder for different segmentation tasks. To evaluate HybPromptSeg, we construct two benchmarks: a single-modality multi-task (SMMT) benchmark for evaluating task discrimination under shared-modality conditions, and a multi-modality multi-task (MMMT) benchmark for evaluating robustness under cross-modality variations. Experimental results demonstrate that HybPromptSeg achieves the best performance among the evaluated unified multi-task models on both benchmarks. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/nnnsjtu/HybSeg.

title: Structured feature disentanglement for high-fidelity unified brain MRI synthesis.
abstract: Multisequence Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) provides a more reliable diagnosis in clinical applications through complementary information across sequences. However, in practice, the absence of certain MR sequences is a common problem that can lead to inconsistent analysis results. In this work, we propose a novel unified framework for synthesizing multisequence MR images, called hybrid-fusion GAN (HF-GAN). The fundamental mechanism of this work is structured feature disentanglement, which aligns the design of the architecture with the complexity of the features. A powerful many-to-one stream is constructed for the extraction of complex complementary features, while utilizing parallel, one-to-one streams to process modality-specific information. A channel attention-based fusion module (CAFF) dynamically integrates these disentangled features as a universal anatomical map into a common latent space. Then, a modality infuser transforms the features to generate the target sequence. We validated our framework on public datasets of both healthy and pathological brain MRI. Quantitative and qualitative results show that HF-GAN achieves state-of-the-art performance, with our 2D slice-based framework notably yielding highly competitive and efficient results compared to a leading 3D volumetric model. Furthermore, the utilization of HF-GAN for data imputation substantially improves the performance of the downstream brain tumor segmentation task, demonstrating its clinical relevance. Our source code is available on https://github.com/SSTDV-Project/HF-GAN.

title: FDG-PET in Lymphoma: The Deauville Era and Beyond.
abstract: FDG-positron emission tomography (PET) has augmented lymphoma imaging from morphology-based assessment to functional metabolic evaluation. The introduction of the Deauville five-point scale and its incorporation into the Lugano classification marked the beginning of the "Deauville era" providing a standardized staging and response assessment, enabling risk adapted therapy and prognostication in FDG-avid lymphomas and detection of histologic transformation in lymphomas with low FDG uptake. Beyond visual interpretation, volumetric biomarkers such as metabolic tumor volume and total lesion glycolysis have demonstrated important prognostic value. Emerging Artificial Intelligence applications are further expanding the role of FDG-PET in lymphoma management.

title: Role of PET/Computed Tomography in Gynecologic and Ovarian Malignancies.
abstract: This article reviews the current status of 2-[ 18 F]fluoro-2-deoxy-d-glucose PET/computed tomography (CT) and FDG PET/MR imaging in comparison to other widely available imaging modalities with the aim to guide in the selection of the most appropriate imaging modality for initial diagnosis, staging, planning optimal treatment, and demonstrating recurrence in patients with suspected or known gynecologic malignancies according to the stage at presentation.

title: FDG-PET in Cognitive Impairment and Dementia.
abstract: Neuroimaging is crucial in early and accurate assessment of diagnosis, prognosis, and therapy optimization in patients with declining cognitive abilities. Imaging modalities now available for clinical indications related to neurodegenerative processes include Computed Tomography (CT), MR imaging, and PET imaging with 6 positron-emitting radiotracers approved at this time by the US Food and Drug Administration. The central focus of this article is the role of FDG-PET in clinical and research applications of patients with cognitive problems, and how the derived information may be effectively integrated with information acquired from other neuroimaging modalities.

title: Fluorodeoxyglucose-PET in Myocardial Viability and Ischemic Heart Disease.
abstract: Assessment of myocardial viability remains pivotal in managing patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy and left ventricular dysfunction. Fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG)-PET is the reference standard for evaluating myocardial metabolic viability, enabling identification of dysfunctional yet salvageable myocardium that may benefit from revascularization. This review summarizes the pathophysiological basis, imaging protocols, interpretation strategies, and clinical evidence supporting FDG-PET for myocardial viability assessment. Particular emphasis is placed on recent advancements, including quantitative imaging, hybrid PET/computed tomography and PET/MR imaging systems, artificial intelligence, radiomics, and emerging molecular tracers. Future directions and ongoing challenges in viability imaging are also discussed.

title: 18 F-Fluorodeoxyglucose PET in Rheumatologic and Autoimmune Disorders.
abstract: FDG PET detects the silent inflammation of autoimmune and rheumatologic diseases even before tissue damage, as activated leukocytes overexpress glucose transporters. It has an important role in large vessel vasculitis which includes early diagnosis, disease monitoring and response assessment to treatment. In inflammatory arthritides, it quantifies synovitis and enthesitis and detects early treatment response. In connective tissue and immunoglobulin G4 related diseases, whole body imaging maps silent disease, helps exclude malignancy, and guides biopsy. It is central to cardiac sarcoidosis and an early test in fever of unknown origin.

title: 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT in Sepsis.
abstract: 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tompgraphy/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) has emerged as a valuable whole-body metabolic imaging modality in sepsis and related systemic infectious disorders. Exploiting increased glucose metabolism in activated inflammatory cells, it facilitates localization of occult infective foci, detection of septic embolization, and guidance of source control when conventional investigations are inconclusive. Evidence demonstrates high diagnostic yield and meaningful impact on clinical management, particularly in sepsis of unknown origin and high-risk bacteraemia. However, diagnostic accuracy depends on appropriate patient preparation and timing. This review summarizes current evidence, practical challenges, emerging applications, and future research priorities for integrating 18F-FDG PET/CT into sepsis care.

title: Valuable Role of Fluorodeoxyglucose-PET in Therapeutic Decision Making and Theranostics of Neurologic Disorders in Conjunction with Non-Fluorodeoxyglucose Tracers.
abstract: Brain ¹⁸F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) is an important functional imaging modality for evaluating glucose metabolism. Over time, it has been observed that various metabolic patterns can support diagnoses, inform prognosis, guide therapeutic decision-making, and assess treatment response. Clinical applications span seizures, brain tumors, traumatic brain injury, neuroinflammatory and infectious disorders, neurodegenerative diseases, and other chronic neurological conditions. Although FDG is not itself a theranostic radiopharmaceutical, its ability to characterize metabolism may contribute to treatment planning, particularly in molecularly targeted neuro-oncology. This chapter reviews established and investigational applications of brain FDG-PET, emphasizing disease characterization, therapeutic selection, and response assessment.

title: A decade of image-guided pleural biopsies: a multicentre retrospective study assessing diagnostic yield and complication rate.
abstract: Aim Pleural disease is common, with diagnostic options including pleural effusion cytology and pleural biopsy, either by local anaesthetic thoracoscopy (LAT) or image-guided biopsy. LAT facilitates multiregion sampling and simultaneous effusion management but may not be feasible with a loculated pleural space. Using long term local data, we assessed the diagnostic yield (DY) and complications associated with ultrasound-guided pleural biopsy (USGPB) and computed tomography-guided pleural biopsy (CTGPB). Materials and methods We performed a retrospective multicentre cohort study across 6 hospitals, retrieving data regarding USGPB and CTGPB performed in these hospitals between 01/01/13 and 31/03/23 using study code and key word searches. Patient demographics, pathology, final diagnosis (by biopsy or consensus diagnosis), and complications were recorded. Results A total of 194 CTGPBs were performed; 166/194 were diagnostic (DY 85.6%). 7/194 (3.6%) had a peri-procedural pneumothorax on CT, but none required intervention. For diagnosis of pleural malignancy, the sensitivity of CTGPB was 93.9% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 88.9%-97.0%), specificity 100% (89.1%-100%), positive predictive value (PPV) 100% (97.6-100%) and negative predictive value (NPV) 76.2 (63.7-85.4%). Ninty-three USGPBs were performed, all without post-procedural pneumothorax; 83/93 were diagnostic (DY: 89.2%). For pleural malignancy diagnosis, sensitivity of USGPB was 94.1% (95% CI: 84.5%-97.7%), specificity 100% (59.0%-100%), PPV 100% (94.6%-100%) and NPV 60.0% (37.5%-76.5%). Conclusion CTGPB and USGPB are safe and accurate for diagnosis of pleural malignancy in cases where LAT is not available or feasible.

title: Change in left atrioventricular coupling index from acute to chronic phases for prediction of major adverse cardiac events after myocardial infarction.
abstract: Aim Previous studies confirmed the usability of the left atrioventricular coupling index (LACI) to enhance risk stratification of cardiovascular adverse events in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). We intend to study the prognostic value of the change in LACI (ΔLACI) from the acute to the chronic phases to predict major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in an AMI patient cohort. Materials and methods A total of 264 patients following AMI were included in a secondary analysis. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed in the acute and chronic stages. LACI was defined by the ratio of left atrial to left ventricular end-diastolic volumes. MACE, including all-cause mortality, reinfarction, or heart failure after the follow-up examination (52 [interquartile range {IQR}: 47-61] months after AMI), was defined as the primary endpoint. Results Among the 264 participants (median age, 59 years [IQR 50-66]; 229 men), MACE occurred in 41 patients over 52 months after the first imaging. LACI was higher in patients with MACE (P< 0.001). The Youden Index identified a LACI cut-off at 24% and a ΔLACI cut-off at 0.02%/month (both P < 0.001) to classify high-risk patients. After adjusting for multivariate models, ΔLACI (model 1, hazard ratio [HR]: 0.46, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.36-0.60; model 2, HR: 0.62, 95% CI: 0.50-0.78; both P < 0.001) was an independent predictor of MACE. ΔLACI enabled further risk stratification in AMI (LACI > 24%, P < 0.001; LACI < 24%, P = 0.013). Conclusion LACI and ΔLACI provide superior prognostic value for MACE in AMI patients. ΔLACI provides incremental prognostic value beyond baseline LACI.

title: Sex-based variability of water-equivalent diameter (Dw) and dosimetric parameters in adult head computed tomography (CT): implications for protocol optimisation.
abstract: Aim The water-equivalent diameter (Dw) is increasingly used to express patient size in computed tomography (CT). Sex-related differences in Dw are documented in the chest and abdomen, but data for adult head CT remain scarce. The aims of this study were to compare Dw and dosimetric parameters (tube current-time product [mAs], volume computed tomography dose index [CTDIvol], size-specific dose estimates based on water-equivalent diameter [SSDEw], dose-length product [DLP], effective dose [EDw]) between men and women undergoing adult noncontrast head CT and to assess the relationship of Dw with mAs and SSDEw. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 109 adult noncontrast head CT examinations (67 men and 42 women) performed with a standardised protocol on a 16-slice CT. Dw and dose indices were calculated using automated segmentation and compared between sexes (independent t-test); relationships were assessed by linear regression. Results No significant differences were found between sexes for Dw, mAs, CTDIvol, or SSDEw (all P > 0.05). DLP and EDw were slightly higher in men (P = 0.0337 and P = 0.0445), mainly owing to larger Dw and scan lengths. Dw correlated positively with mAs (women r = 0.57; men r = 0.46; P < 0.001) and SSDEw (women r = 0.52; men r = 0.38; P ≤ 0.002). Conclusion In this single-centre series, limited intersex variability in adult head CT dose metrics supports standardised protocols irrespective of sex. Dw is most valuable for dose audit, quality control, and identification of outlying examinations; its contribution to optimisation, which also requires image quality assessment, should be confirmed in prospective multicentre studies.

originalAbstract:
Aim

The water-equivalent diameter (Dw) is increasingly used to express patient size in computed tomography (CT). Sex-related differences in Dw are documented in the chest and abdomen, but data for adult head CT remain scarce. The aims of this study were to compare Dw and dosimetric parameters (tube current-time product [mAs], volume computed tomography dose index [CTDIvol], size-specific dose estimates based on water-equivalent diameter [SSDEw], dose-length product [DLP], effective dose [EDw]) between men and women undergoing adult noncontrast head CT and to assess the relationship of Dw with mAs and SSDEw.

Materials and methods

This retrospective study included 109 adult noncontrast head CT examinations (67 men and 42 women) performed with a standardised protocol on a 16-slice CT. Dw and dose indices were calculated using automated segmentation and compared between sexes (independent t-test); relationships were assessed by linear regression.

Results

No significant differences were found between sexes for Dw, mAs, CTDIvol, or SSDEw (all P > 0.05). DLP and EDw were slightly higher in men (P = 0.0337 and P = 0.0445), mainly owing to larger Dw and scan lengths. Dw correlated positively with mAs (women r = 0.57; men r = 0.46; P < 0.001) and SSDEw (women r = 0.52; men r = 0.38; P ≤ 0.002).

Conclusion

In this single-centre series, limited intersex variability in adult head CT dose metrics supports standardised protocols irrespective of sex. Dw is most valuable for dose audit, quality control, and identification of outlying examinations; its contribution to optimisation, which also requires image quality assessment, should be confirmed in prospective multicentre studies.

title: When is 4 Gy enough? Defining dose sufficiency and durable control in indolent B-cell lymphoma.
abstract: Ultra-low-dose radiotherapy, most commonly delivered as 4 Gy in two fractions (2 Gy × 2), is an established low-burden approach for radiosensitive indolent B-cell lymphoma. Its use as stand-alone definitive local therapy is constrained by a persistent gap between early tumor regression and durable local control. This review examines when 4 Gy should be considered sufficient by integrating clinical intent, lesion biology, response assessment, immune context, and emerging biomarkers. We distinguish its use as stand-alone local treatment, palliation, response-adapted de-escalation, and immune-integrated strategies. Across these settings, early response indicates radiosensitivity but does not prove lesion sterilization or equivalence to standard-dose radiotherapy. Dose sufficiency depends on durable in-field control, tumor burden, anatomical definition, reassessment reliability, feasibility of salvage, and the consequences of local failure. Immune and cellular combinations may extend the value of 4 Gy beyond local cytoreduction, but the contribution of irradiation should be tested separately from systemic or intratumoral partners. PET response, MRD, ctDNA, and immune correlates may help distinguish transient cytoreduction from durable clearance and local response from patient-level disease control. At present, these biomarkers are better suited to trial design and mechanistic validation than to routine dose selection. Future studies should move beyond response rates and define decision rules that link early response, immune modulation, biomarker dynamics, lesion-level durability, salvageability, and cumulative treatment burden.

title: Multimodal AI for early lung cancer detection: from LDCT to clinical and molecular integration.
abstract: Low‑dose computed tomography (LDCT) is the established screening backbone for lung cancer in high‑risk populations. However, its clinical value depends on a complete pathway, including eligibility assessment, image acquisition, nodule interpretation, follow‑up, referral, quality assurance, and harm reduction, and not on image detection alone. Artificial intelligence (AI), radiomics, clinical‑risk models, and blood‑ or breath‑based biomarkers are being investigated as tools to improve decisions within that pathway. This narrative, state‑of‑the‑art translational review synthesizes evidence on AI‑enabled integration of clinical risk, LDCT‑derived imaging features, radiomics, longitudinal imaging, and molecular or experimental biomarkers for early lung cancer detection and pulmonary nodule triage. AI‑enabled integration may improve defined decisions within the LDCT pathway, most plausibly pulmonary nodule triage. To distinguish genuine decision support from simple data fusion, this review applies a five‑tier framework: data aggregation, diagnostic enrichment, risk stratification, threshold‑based triage, and pathway‑level decision support across all modalities and studies. Within this framework, cell‑free DNA (cfDNA) methylation and cfDNA fragmentomics occupy a higher translational tier than autoantibodies, generic serum markers, breathomics, or metabolomics, because their signals have a coherent biological basis and they have been tested in multimodal nodule‑triage studies with external validation. AI is best understood as an integrative decision layer within LDCT‑centered pathways. Its value depends on whether it supports calibrated, fair, and actionable decisions, not on discrimination alone. The guiding question of this review is not about a general comparison between AI and biomarkers. Rather, it is about identifying which data layer most benefits each particular decision, pinpointing the exact stage of the LDCT pathway where that decision occurs, and evaluating that benefit based on rigorous evidence of calibration, safety, and net clinical benefit.

title: Drastic muscle wasting following surgery is a strong predictor of prognosis in early-stage pancreatic cancer-a Taiwanese multicenter cohort study.
abstract: Objective To clarify the impact of preoperative sarcopenia and muscle wasting postoperative on the short- and long-term outcomes following pancreatectomy in resectable pancreatic cancer (PC) patients. Summary background data Previous studies revealed that sarcopenia, defined as generalized loss of skeletal muscle mass, was a poor prognosis factor following surgery. However, research focus on postoperative muscle wasting and their influences on the prognosis in resectable PC was very limited. Methods Retrospective analysis was performed for 284 early-stage PC patients who underwent pancreatic resection in two medical centers. Preoperative psoas major area and the degree of muscle reduction postoperative 3 months were calculated by computed tomography to define sarcopenia and drastic muscle wasting. Patients were assigned to 2 groups based on the presence or absence of sarcopenia or drastic muscle wasting and compared for postoperative morbidity and survival rate. Results Sarcopenia was present in 149 of 284 patients (52.4%), and a total of 88 patients (31.0%) developed muscle wasting of over 17% postoperatively. Compared with non-sarcopenia group, patients with sarcopenia had significantly greater incidence of overall or major morbidity (P = 0.001; P = 0.038, respectively), while sarcopenia status didn't correlate with poor-long term survival (DFS, P = 0.812; OS, P = 0.238). Surprisingly, patients presented drastic muscle wasting displayed poor DFS (P < 0.001) and OS (P < 0.001) and were found to be independent predictors of unfavorable DFS (P = 0.005) and OS (P < 0.001) after adjusting for clinicopathologic parameters. Conclusions Sarcopenia preoperative is associated with higher risk of morbidity. Moreover, the concept of assessment in wasting muscle quantity following pancreatectomy is essential for accurate long-term prognosis in resectable PC patients.

title: Interpretable CT-based radiomics nomogram integrating clinical and semantic features for preoperative grading of pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms: a shap-based analysis.
abstract: Preoperative grading of pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (PNENs) is crucial for personalized management. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine-learning framework based on CT imaging to predict PNENs pathological grades. We retrospectively analyzed 125 patients with pathologically confirmed PNENs, divided into training and test cohorts. A comprehensive radiomics pipeline was implemented, involving the extraction of high-dimensional features from CT images. We constructed three predictive models: a clinical model, a radiomics model, and a fusion model. To ensure methodological robustness, seven machine-learning algorithms were employed and cross-validated to identify the optimal classifier. Furthermore, the SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) method was utilized to decode the "black box" of the radiomics signature. The fusion model-integrating CT radiomic signatures with semantic hallmarks-consistently outperformed the standalone clinical and radiomics models, achieving a superior AUC of 0.891 in the validation cohort. SHAP analysis revealed that microscopic texture complexity (e.g., Zone Entropy) and macro-geometric irregularity (e.g., Sphericity) were the dominant predictors, aligning with the biological aggressiveness of high-grade lesions. By integrating multi-dimensional CT features with a rigorous machine-learning consensus, our study provides a highly accurate and interpretable "virtual biopsy" tool.

title: CT-guided iodine-125 brachytherapy for advanced thymic epithelial tumors: a preliminary observational study.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to provide a preliminary description of the application of CT-guided iodine-125 ( 125 I) seed implantation, a form of brachytherapy, in patients with advanced or recurrent thymic epithelial tumors (TETs). Methods We retrospectively reviewed seven patients with advanced or recurrent TETs who underwent CT-guided 125 I seed implantation. Based on the extent of disease at presentation, one patient had widespread distant metastases, while the remaining six had localized lesions. Treatment planning was performed using a treatment planning system(TPS, Beijing Astro Technology Co., Ltd.) with a prescribed dose of 60-70 Gy. Follow-up evaluations included regular contrast-enhanced CT scans. Tumor response was assessed according to RECIST 1.1 criteria, and safety was evaluated using CTCAE v5.0. Results A total of 12 lesions were treated across seven patients. All procedures were technically successful. Over a median follow-up of 46 months (range: 9-69 months),four patients (57.1%) attained a complete response (CR) and three patients (42.9%) attained a partial response (PR) at the patient level. Patient-level response was defined by composite assessment of all target lesions. At the lesion level, six lesions (50%) demonstrated a CR and six lesions (50%) demonstrated a partial response PR. Notably, lesion-level observations are statistically non-independent given that half of treated lesions derived from a single patient. Complications included pneumothorax in three patients (one of whom required drainage) and grade 1 radiation pneumonitis in one patient; all adverse events resolved without long-term sequelae. No severe radiation-related toxicities (e.g., pericarditis) were observed. In a descriptive subgroup excluding the patient with widespread metastases, four of six patients achieved CR and two achieved PR; no local progression was documented during available follow-up, but this finding remains descriptive and non-comparative. Conclusion CT-guided ¹²⁵I radioactive seed implantation appears feasible and well-tolerated in patients with advanced or recurrent TETs. The observed objective tumour responses and toxicity profile are hypothesis-generating but must be interpreted with caution given the very small sample size, heterogeneous cohort, non-independent lesion-level data, and lack of a control group. This preliminary study cannot establish durable local control or superiority over external beam radiotherapy. Further larger, prospective studies with standardized dosimetry and time-to-event endpoints are warranted.

title: Peri-urethral calcifications as a potential biomarker for acute genitourinary toxicity following prostate stereotactic body radiotherapy.
abstract: Background and objectives Peri-urethral calcifications (PUCs) are readily identifiable on planning computed tomography (CT) and may reflect chronic inflammation, fibrosis, and reduced peri-urethral tissue compliance. We evaluated whether baseline PUCs are associated with acute genitourinary (GU) toxicity following prostate stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT). Methods We retrospectively analyzed 60 consecutive patients with localized prostate adenocarcinoma treated with definitive SBRT between June 2023 and February 2026. PUCs were assessed on non-contrast planning CT using predefined criteria by blinded observers. The primary endpoint was acute grade ≥ 2 GU toxicity occurring during treatment or within 90 days, graded according to CTCAE v5. Associations with toxicity were evaluated using logistic regression, with Firth penalized regression used for multivariable analysis. Results PUCs were identified in 17 patients (28.3%). Interobserver agreement was high (93.3%; Cohen's κ = 0.84). Overall, 21 patients (35%) developed acute grade ≥ 2 GU toxicity, including three (5%) with grade ≥ 3 toxicity. Acute grade ≥ 2 GU toxicity occurred significantly more frequently in patients with PUCs than in those without PUCs (64.7% vs 23.3%; OR 6.05, 95% CI 1.78-20.51; P = 0.006). After adjustment for baseline International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), PUCs remained independently associated with toxicity (adjusted OR 6.90, 95% CI 1.97-27.96; P = 0.002). Baseline IPSS was also independently associated with toxicity (adjusted OR 1.13 per point; P = 0.008). Conclusion PUCs on routine planning CT were independently associated with acute grade ≥ 2 GU toxicity after prostate SBRT. If externally validated, PUC assessment may provide a simple, cost-neutral imaging biomarker for pretreatment urinary toxicity risk stratification.

title: Development and validation of a cumulative risk model and assessment tool for radiation-induced hypothyroidism in head and neck cancer: a multicentre study.
abstract: Objectives Radiation-induced hypothyroidism (RIHT) is a common late toxicity after head and neck radiotherapy. We aimed to develop and externally validate a multimodal Cox model for patient-specific cumulative RIHT risk assessment. Materials & methods This retrospective multicentre study included 1407 patients across four cohorts. The model was developed in the training cohort and externally validated in three independent cohorts. Candidate predictors included CT radiomics, dosiomics, dose-volume histogram parameters, and clinical variables. A multimodal Cox model was developed and used to estimate cumulative risks across time horizons. Temporal risk groups were derived from predicted 3- and 7-year risks. Results A total of 1407 patients (mean age, 55.4 ± 13.8 years; 1027 men) were evaluated and RIHT occurred in 694 (49.3%). The final model integrated three CT radiomics features, four dosiomics features, mean thyroid dose, age and N stage. It achieved C-index/overall AUC values of 0.714/0.765 in the development cohort and 0.725/0.800, 0.680/0.754, and 0.627/0.690 in the three external validation cohorts. Four temporal risk groups had RIHT event rates of 21.7%, 46.1%, 58.3%, and 71.8%, with significant differences in RIHT-free survival (log-rank p < 0.001). The model was packaged as an open-source software tool for individualised risk assessment. Conclusion The externally validated multimodal Cox model provided time-resolved, patient-specific RIHT risk estimates and temporal risk stratification using routinely available radiotherapy-planning data.

title: Metastasis-directed therapy in addition to definitive locoregional radiotherapy for De novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background De novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (mNPC) carries a poor prognosis with systemic therapy alone. Locoregional radiotherapy (LRRT) improves survival in chemotherapy-responsive patients, but the incremental role of metastasis-directed therapy (MDT) remains undefined. Methods This retrospective cohort included 54 patients with de novo mNPC treated between 2013 and 2024 at a tertiary cancer centre. All received platinum-based induction chemotherapy followed by definitive LRRT; selected patients underwent MDT to metastatic sites. Overall survival (OS), recurrence-free survival (RFS) and distant recurrence-free survival (DRFS) were estimated by Kaplan-Meier methods, with Cox regression for univariable and multivariable analysis. Results At a median follow-up of 27 months, 2-year OS, RFS and DRFS were 67.5%, 45.4% and 52.7%. MDT was associated with improved 2-year OS (92.3% vs 55.2%; p = 0.0069), RFS (81.9% vs 28.2%; p < 0.001) and DRFS (93.8% vs 35.0%; p < 0.001). On multivariable analysis MDT remained associated with improved RFS (HR 0.27, 95% CI 0.08-0.98; p = 0.047), with consistent estimates in a 2-month landmark analysis (HR 0.26, 95% CI 0.075-0.90) and with MDT modelled as a time-varying covariate (HR 0.17, 95% CI 0.040-0.76); the association with OS was not statistically significant (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.06-1.13; p = 0.072). Oligometastatic disease was more frequent among patients receiving MDT (88% vs 41%). The association was most evident in the oligometastatic subgroup. In exploratory analyses, detectable post-treatment plasma EBV DNA and elevated post-LRRT PET SUV were associated with inferior survival. Conclusion In chemotherapy-responsive de novo mNPC treated with definitive LRRT, consolidative MDT was associated with improved disease control in multivariable, landmark and time-varying analyses, with a directionally consistent but non-significant association with OS. As residual confounding cannot be excluded, these findings support prospective evaluation in selected patients.

title: Association of CT-detected central airway obstruction with clinical airway events and survival in patients receiving palliative thoracic radiotherapy.
abstract: Introduction Malignant central airway obstruction results in significant morbidity and mortality, and is often detected late despite preceding evidence on Computed Tomography (CT) imaging. We evaluated whether CT-detected central airway obstruction is associated with clinical airway events and overall survival (OS). Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study of patients receiving palliative thoracic radiotherapy from 2015 to 2023. A 3D central airway model was automatically segmented from CT scans, and a thoracic radiologist scored each airway to the lobar level as patent or obstructed. The primary outcome was OS. Secondary outcomes were clinical airway events (symptomatic obstruction or hemorrhage) and catastrophic (CTCAE v5 ≥ III) clinical airway events. The associations of obstruction with survival and clinical airway events were assessed with Cox and logistic regression analyses, with multivariable analyses incorporating age, sex, ECOG performance status, primary disease site, and cancer stage. Results Among 280 included patients, 174 had all central airways patent and 106 had central airway obstruction on CT. The presence of any central airway obstruction was associated with shorter OS in univariable (HR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.09,1.87) but not multivariable (HR: 1.29; 95% CI: 0.97,1.72) analyses. Central airway obstruction was associated with higher odds of clinical airway events (OR: 2.60; 95% CI: 1.56,4.40) on multivariable analysis. The number of obstructed airways detected on imaging was associated with progressively higher odds of any clinical airway events (OR: 1.48; 95% CI: 1.20,1.88) and catastrophic airway events (OR:1.31; 95% CI: 1.07,1.61) in multivariable analyses. Obstruction of the trachea, left or right main bronchi was associated with the highest odds of catastrophic airway events (OR: 3.77; 95% CI: 1.45,9.94) on multivariable analysis. Conclusions CT-detected proximal airway obstruction is associated with subsequent clinical airway events in patients undergoing palliative thoracic radiotherapy. Structured assessment of routine CT imaging may improve early intervention and risk stratification.

title: ESTRO consensus recommendations: target volume and organ at risk delineation in rectal endoluminal high dose rate brachytherapy.
abstract: Background and purpose Lack of international guidelines is hampering treatment quality and progress in the field of rectal endoluminal high dose rate brachytherapy (EHB). Standardisation of dose reporting would allow for better comparison of clinical results between patient cohorts and allow tumour control and normal tissue complication probability modelling. This work presents consensus recommendations for target volume and organs at risk (OAR) delineation in rectal EHB to support standardised dose reporting, for which consistent delineation is a prerequisite. Materials and methods Recommendations were developed according to the AGREE II instrument, using a modified Delphi approach. The process included selection of international experts, a survey on current practices, delineation of three patient cases, and three consensus meetings to discuss the findings and formulate recommendations. Results The expert group included 30 members from nine countries. The survey and first delineation round showed marked variation in treatment preparation and in the definition and delineation of target volumes and OARs. Consensus was reached on prerequisites for adequate delineation. Target volumes for dose reporting were defined: GTV primary at the time of EHB (GTVp_BT), an evaluation structure (GTVp_BT_ev05), and any macroscopic lymph nodes at the time of EHB (GTVn_BT). Recommendations for OAR selection and delineation were also established. Conclusion The GI GEC working group of GEC-ESTRO has developed consensus recommendations for target volume definition and OAR delineation in rectal EHB. These recommendations will be implemented in clinical practice. The proposed structures provide a foundation for standardised dose reporting, independent of local prescription practices.

title: Deep and ultra-deep PSA responses as prognostic biomarkers in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. A systematic review and implications for treatment personalization.
abstract: Background Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) exhibits heterogeneous outcomes despite standard androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and widespread first-line intensification with androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) and/or docetaxel. Simple, widely accessible biomarkers are needed to individualize care (intensification vs de-intensification). We systematically reviewed the prognostic value of post-therapy PSA dynamics-particularly deep (≤ 0.2 ng/mL) and ultra-deep (≤ 0.02 ng/mL) PSA responses-and their potential role to inform future predictive strategies. Methods We searched MEDLINE and EMBASE for randomized trials and observational studies in mHSPC treated with ADT alone or combined with chemotherapy, ARPIs and/or radiotherapy to the primary tumor. Primary outcomes were overall survival (OS), radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS)/PFS, and time to castration resistance (TTCR). Post-therapy PSA assessment windows varied across studies (typically 3-7 months), and the anchoring time point was either ADT initiation or randomization (with variable prior ADT exposure). In addition, we reviewed clinicaltrials.gov for PSA-guided treatment adaptative ongoing clinical trials. Results Of 785 records identified, 65 references met the eligibility criteria, corresponding to 16 phase III randomized trials, 1 meta-analysis and 42 retrospective studies. The phase III trials evaluated different treatment strategies, including ADT alone, ADT plus docetaxel, ADT plus androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs; apalutamide, abiraterone, darolutamide, enzalutamide, or rezvilutamide), and triplet therapy. Across trials, deep and ultradeep early PSA responses were consistently associated with longer rPFS and OS. Conversely, higher PSA nadirs or incomplete early PSA responses predicted earlier progression and shorter survival. Observational cohorts showed concordant findings. In addition, eight landmark PSA-guided adaptive randomized clinical trials (seven ongoing or planned and one recently reported) were summarized, including treatment de-escalation strategies for patients with optimal PSA responses and treatment intensification strategies for those with suboptimal PSA responses. Conclusions Achieving a deep or ultra-deep PSA response after starting systemic therapy is a robust and affordable prognostic indicator in mHSPC. Harmonization of PSA assessment windows and thresholds is crucial. Ongoing randomized trials will help to understand its utility for treatment personalization.

We searched MEDLINE and EMBASE for randomized trials and observational studies in mHSPC treated with ADT alone or combined with chemotherapy, ARPIs and/or radiotherapy to the primary tumor. Primary outcomes were overall survival (OS), radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS)/PFS, and time to castration resistance (TTCR). Post-therapy PSA assessment windows varied across studies (typically 3-7 months), and the anchoring time point was either ADT initiation or randomization (with variable prior ADT exposure). In addition, we reviewed clinicaltrials.gov for PSA-guided treatment adaptative ongoing clinical trials.

Results

Of 785 records identified, 65 references met the eligibility criteria, corresponding to 16 phase III randomized trials, 1 meta-analysis and 42 retrospective studies. The phase III trials evaluated different treatment strategies, including ADT alone, ADT plus docetaxel, ADT plus androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs; apalutamide, abiraterone, darolutamide, enzalutamide, or rezvilutamide), and triplet therapy. Across trials, deep and ultradeep early PSA responses were consistently associated with longer rPFS and OS. Conversely, higher PSA nadirs or incomplete early PSA responses predicted earlier progression and shorter survival. Observational cohorts showed concordant findings. In addition, eight landmark PSA-guided adaptive randomized clinical trials (seven ongoing or planned and one recently reported) were summarized, including treatment de-escalation strategies for patients with optimal PSA responses and treatment intensification strategies for those with suboptimal PSA responses.

Conclusions

Achieving a deep or ultra-deep PSA response after starting systemic therapy is a robust and affordable prognostic indicator in mHSPC. Harmonization of PSA assessment windows and thresholds is crucial. Ongoing randomized trials will help to understand its utility for treatment personalization.

title: Gray matter abnormalities associated with long-term opium use: A voxel-based morphometry study.
abstract: Chronic raw opium use can result in opioid use disorder (OUD). Although voxel-based morphometry (VBM) studies have demonstrated decreased gray matter volume (GMV) in heroin-induced OUD, the structural impacts of long-term raw opium consumption remain poorly understood. This study investigated GMV alterations in men with opium-induced OUD and their association with use duration. High-resolution T1-weighted MRI scans were acquired from 28 men with opium-induced OUD (mean use duration 17.89 ± 5.85 years) receiving opium tincture maintenance and 25 age- and education-matched healthy male controls. Whole-brain VBM (CAT12/SPM12) was controlled for age, total intracranial volume, and nicotine use. Analysis used a voxel-level uncorrected threshold of p < 0.05 with cluster-level FDR correction (p < 0.05), along with stricter thresholds (uncorrected p < 0.001, TFCE with FWE), and small-volume correction (SVC). Partial correlation and multiple linear regression investigated clinical associations. Whole-brain analysis identified a left-hemisphere cluster of reduced GMV (cluster-level FDR-corrected p = 0.009). No clusters survived p < 0.001 or TFCE with FWE correction. Reductions in the left insula, inferior frontal gyrus, and parahippocampal gyrus remained significant after SVC. Left insula GMV was negatively associated with duration of opium use (partial r = -0.45, p = 0.027; β = -0.48, p = 0.027 in regression). Prolonged raw opium use is associated with decreased GMV in areas involved in craving and impulse control. Given that the whole-brain findings were not confirmed by more stringent statistical approaches, the results should be considered exploratory and necessitate replication in larger samples.

title: Effectiveness of technology-enabled teleophthalmology and emerging retinal imaging techniques for diabetic retinopathy screening: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Introduction Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a major microvascular complication of diabetes and causes preventable visual loss. Technology-enabled screening can extend retinal assessment beyond specialist settings and strengthen screening, referral, and follow-up across diabetes care pathways. Methods We systematically reviewed randomized and non-randomized implementation studies, diagnostic-accuracy and comparative retinal-imaging studies, and economic evaluations of technology-enabled DR screening. PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched from inception to 23 May 2026 without language restriction. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Random-effects meta-analyses synthesized comparative and proportional outcomes, and GRADE assessed certainty. Results Thirty-three studies were included. Teleophthalmology increased DR screening uptake/completion versus usual care or pre-implementation practice (RR 1.966, 95% CI 1.451-2.664; I 2 = 75.2%) and improved adherence to recommended eye care (OR 2.464, 95% CI 1.477-4.112; I 2 = 66.47%). The pooled ungradable-image rate was 7.4% (95% CI 3.0%-17.1%; I 2 = 59.17%). Advanced retinal imaging showed pooled sensitivity of 97.59% (95% CI 94.50%-100.00%; I 2 = 0%) and specificity of 91.22% (95% CI 78.46%-100.00%; I 2 = 88.7%) for prespecified vascular lesion detection. OCTA demonstrated a pooled eye-level retinal neovascularization detection yield of 63.6% (95% CI 49.9%-75.4%; I 2 = 46.29%). Economic evaluations supported cost-effective or cost-saving technology-enabled screening across assessed health systems. Conclusion Technology-enabled DR care improves screening participation, adherence, and health-system efficiency, supporting integration of teleophthalmology and advanced imaging into scalable diabetes complication-management pathways.

title: The evolving role of cardiac CT: Emerging technologies and clinical impact.
abstract: Cardiac computed tomography (CT) has progressed from a non-invasive test primarily used to exclude obstructive coronary artery disease into a comprehensive cardiovascular imaging platform for coronary artery disease, myocardial disease, valvular heart disease, and structural heart disease. Coronary CT angiography (CCTA) is now endorsed as a first-line test in appropriately selected patients with stable chest pain or suspected chronic coronary syndromes because it can exclude obstructive disease, depict coronary atherosclerotic burden, support preventive treatment, and inform referral for invasive coronary angiography. At the same time, contemporary cardiac CT is moving beyond luminal stenosis. CT-derived fractional flow reserve and myocardial CT perfusion add a functional assessment of ischemia, whereas late iodine enhancement, CT-derived extracellular volume fraction, myocardial strain, and pericoronary fat attenuation index provide information on fibrosis, ventricular mechanics, vascular inflammation, and prognosis. Cardiac CT also has an established role in transcatheter valve therapy, left atrial appendage occlusion, and prosthetic valve assessment by providing a three-dimensional roadmap for device selection, access planning, and complication prediction. Photon-counting detector CT and artificial intelligence are further expanding the capabilities of cardiac CT through higher spatial resolution, spectral quantification, automated segmentation, quantitative plaque analysis, image reconstruction, and structured reporting. This review summarizes the evidence, technical foundations, clinical applications, and implementation challenges of contemporary cardiac CT, with an emphasis on its transition toward a decision-making platform for personalized cardiovascular care.

title: A robust biomarker combining radiomic and CA19.9 information to predict distant relapse-free survival after radiochemotherapy in pancreatic cancer.
abstract: Background The radiomic feature Statistical Percentile 10% (p10%), extracted from [¹⁸F]FDG-PET images, has been previously identified and validated as a robust predictor of distant progression-free survival (DPFS) in unresectable pancreatic cancer (LAPC). This study aimed to maximize its prognostic potential by combining p10% with CA19.9 serum levels and assessing its generalizability across distinct clinical settings. Methods We analyzed 287 LAPC patients treated with chemoradiotherapy (CRT) and a validation cohort of 72 patients enrolled in the CASSANDRA trial (resectable/borderline-resectable PDAC). Cox models combined p10% with CA19.9 levels measured before RT in LAPC patients, and before surgery for CASSANDRA patients. Results p10% was independently prognostic in both cohorts and its integration with CA19.9 significantly improved the prediction. In the LAPC cohort, the combined model achieved C-index=0.71, with median DPFS of 4.0-vs-15.0 months (p<0.0001;HR=3.22). In the pre-surgery setting (CASSANDRA trial), the model showed good rank-order discrimination (C-index=0.65), with median survival of 11.6 months vs not-reached (p=0.0018). However, the calibration slope of 0.54 suggests that absolute risk prediction requires recalibration in the surgical cohort. Conclusions Integrating p10% with CA19.9 provides a broader representation of tumor aggressiveness. The combined biomarkers demonstrate consistent performance across different disease stages supporting their use for treatment personalization.

title: Comparative assessment of ultrasound and bioelectrical impedance analysis for sarcopenia screening in chronic liver disease.
abstract: Background Sarcopenia, primarily defined by low muscle mass (LMM), is associated with worse clinical outcomes in chronic liver disease (CLD). Diagnosis is challenging due to the lack of standardized tools. Ultrasound (US) offers a promising method for muscle mass assessment but requires validation against reference methods like bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA). Aim To evaluate the correlation and agreement between US- and BIA-based muscle measurements and the accuracy of US in identifying sarcopenia in patients with cirrhosis and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods In this prospective observational study, 88 patients with cirrhosis (HCC active or under follow-up) underwent muscle mass assessment by BIA and US of quadriceps and psoas muscles. Analyses included correlations, intraclass correlation (ICC), Bland-Altman plots, and ROC analysis to determine US cut-offs for sarcopenia. Results Quadriceps US indices correlated with BIA-derived ASMM/h² (r = 0.35-0.45, p < 0.01), with high inter-rater reliability (ICC 0.83-0.96). The feather index demonstrated the best discriminative ability (AUROC 0.81, sensitivity 83%, specificity 72%) in this low-prevalence setting. Dual cut-off strategies improved screening value (negative predictive values above 97%). Conclusion Muscle US is a reliable, non-invasive screening tool for sarcopenia (specifically LMM) in CLD patients. Its use can reduce reliance on complex diagnostics, enabling early detection and improved clinical management.

title: A proteome-based classification of paediatric adrenocortical tumours links functional tumour states to clinical outcome and therapeutic vulnerabilities.
abstract: Background Paediatric adrenocortical tumours (pACT) are rare endocrine neoplasms characterised by marked biological heterogeneity and variable clinical behaviour. Current risk stratification relies largely on histopathology and clinical staging, which incompletely capture underlying tumour biology. We aimed to define proteome-based subtypes of pACT and evaluate their biological, clinical, and therapeutic relevance. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, we performed mass spectrometry-based proteomic profiling of 83 pACT and adjacent non-tumour adrenal tissues. Differential abundance analysis, pathway enrichment, consensus clustering, survival analyses, and clinicopathological correlations were performed. A minimal protein classifier was derived using forward feature selection and leave-one-out cross-validation. Cluster-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities were assessed using a curated druggability framework. Findings Tumours displayed profound proteomic differences compared with adjacent non-tumour adrenal cortex, characterised by activation of cholesterol biosynthesis, steroidogenic, MYC, mTORC1, and cell-cycle programs and suppression of extracellular matrix, adhesion, and immune-related pathways. Unsupervised clustering identified four proteome-defined tumour states that only partially overlapped with histopathological diagnosis. These subtypes differed significantly in endocrine phenotype, vascular invasion, Ki67 index, necrosis, and overall survival (log-rank p = 0.00036). Distinct biological programs included stromal-immune-enriched, mitochondrial steroidogenic, IGF/mTOR-driven anabolic, and highly proliferative chromatin-remodelled states. A five-protein classifier (DAAM2, CIP2A, TSC2, PALS2, and P3H1) reproduced cluster assignments with 92.8% leave-one-out cross-validation accuracy. Cluster-specific analyses identified distinct therapeutic target landscapes, including IGF-axis and epigenetic vulnerabilities. Interpretation Proteomic profiling defines biologically and clinically distinct pACT subtypes that provide prognostic information beyond histopathology. This framework enables proteome-based stratification, identifies candidate therapeutic vulnerabilities, and can be approximated by a five-protein classifier. Unsupervised clustering identified four proteome-defined tumour states that only partially overlapped with histopathological diagnosis. These subtypes differed significantly in endocrine phenotype, vascular invasion, Ki67 index, necrosis, and overall survival (log-rank p = 0.00036). Distinct biological programs included stromal-immune-enriched, mitochondrial steroidogenic, IGF/mTOR-driven anabolic, and highly proliferative chromatin-remodelled states. A five-protein classifier (DAAM2, CIP2A, TSC2, PALS2, and P3H1) reproduced cluster assignments with 92.8% leave-one-out cross-validation accuracy. Cluster-specific analyses identified distinct therapeutic target landscapes, including IGF-axis and epigenetic vulnerabilities.

Interpretation

Proteomic profiling defines biologically and clinically distinct pACT subtypes that provide prognostic information beyond histopathology. This framework enables proteome-based stratification, identifies candidate therapeutic vulnerabilities, and can be approximated by a five-protein classifier.

title: NOX4-related ROS couples PET micro- and nanoplastic exposure to JAK2/STAT3 activation in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
abstract: The potential influence of polyethylene terephthalate micro- and nanoplastics (PET-MNPs) on the progression of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) remains insufficiently defined. In this study, environmentally derived PET-MNPs promoted ccRCC cell growth, clonogenic capacity, migration, and invasion, and also accelerated tumor development in subcutaneous and orthotopic models. PET-MNP exposure markedly elevated intracellular ROS and H₂O₂ and preferentially increased NOX4 among the NOX family members examined. Silencing NOX4 attenuated ROS and H₂O₂ accumulation and weakened the associated malignant phenotypes both in vitro and in vivo. Functional rescue further showed that wild-type NOX4, but not the catalytically impaired NOX4-P437H mutant, reinstated oxidative signaling and JAK2/STAT3 activation after NOX4 depletion. Transcriptomic analysis of PET-MNP-responsive genes reversed by NOX4 knockdown highlighted JAK-STAT signaling, which was subsequently narrowed to the JAK2/STAT3 branch by protein screening. JAK2 depletion impaired STAT3 Tyr705 phosphorylation, nuclear localization, and transcriptional activity, whereas STAT3 silencing suppressed PET-MNP-induced tumor-promoting phenotypes. Conversely, constitutively active STAT3 partially restored the effects lost after NOX4 depletion. These results define a NOX4-related ROS-JAK2/STAT3 signaling cascade that contributes to PET-MNP-driven ccRCC progression.

title: Circulating tumor DNA-guided therapeutic strategies for metastatic colorectal cancer patients with multiple small pulmonary-limited nodules: A prospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Small pulmonary nodules (SPNs ≤ 2 cm) in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) had heterogeneous biology and no evidence-based treatment algorithms. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) can detect molecular residual disease (MRD) but lacks prospective validation for treatment guidance in this setting. Methods 70 mCRC patients with exclusively SPNs were assigned to Cohort 1 (≤1 cm) and Cohort 2 (1-2 cm). Tumor-informed ctDNA was detected at baseline, 30 days after optional local treatment or systemic chemotherapy, then every 3 months for 24 months or until progression. Primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Results Baseline ctDNA positivity was 35.5% in Cohort 1 and 66.7% in Cohort 2. In Cohort 1, baseline ctDNA positivity significantly correlated with shorter PFS (median PFS: 3.2 months vs. 9.2 months, P = 0.013), which was not seen in Cohort 2. Systemic chemotherapy was associated with a five-fold higher ctDNA clearance than local treatment alone (63.2 % vs. 12.5 %, P = 0.033). ctDNA clearance was associated with longer median PFS (12.6 months vs. 6.8 months, P = 0.038). Longitudinally, patients with consistently negative ctDNA had significantly longer PFS than the overall population (median PFS: not reached vs. 9.2 months, P = 0.012). ctDNA better predicted extrapulmonary metastases with a median lead time of 5.5 months (range, 2.8-9.2 months) preceding radiographic confirmation and extrapulmonary metastases predicted poorer PFS than intrapulmonary spread (median PFS: 3.5 months vs. 9.9 months, P = 0.005). Conclusions Longitudinal ctDNA monitoring may provide prognostic information and help identify extrapulmonary progression in mCRC patients with SPNs. These exploratory findings require prospective validation before informing clinical treatment decisions.

title: From staging to changing strategy: [ 18 F]FDG PET/MRI's impact on treatment planning in early breast cancer.
abstract: Introduction Accurate staging at diagnosis is essential for optimizing treatment strategies and prognosis in early breast cancer (EBC). [ 18 F]FDG positron emission tomography/magnetic resonance imaging (PET/MRI) is a hybrid imaging modality that enables simultaneous evaluation of locoregional disease and metastatic spread. This study assessed the impact of [ 18 F]FDG PET/MRI on treatment planning in patients with EBC. Methods This unplanned sub-study derives from a prospective, interventional, single-arm clinical trial (SNB vs PET/MRI 2) conducted at San Raffaele University Hospital (Milan) between July 2020 and April 2024 (NCT04829643). Patients with EBC scheduled for primary surgery underwent additional preoperative [ 18 F]FDG PET/MRI. The primary objective was the proportion of patients whose treatment strategy was modified following [ 18 F]FDG PET/MRI findings and multidisciplinary discussion. The secondary objective was the performance of [ 18 F]FDG PET/MRI in detecting multifocal breast cancer compared with standard imaging. Results A total of 264 patients were analyzed. [ 18 F]FDG PET/MRI led to treatment plan modifications 30.7% (81/264, 95% CI: 25.4%-36.5%) of patients. Surgical approach was altered in 23.9% (63/264), while 4.9% (13/264) received primary systemic therapy and 1.9% (5/264) were referred for systemic therapy alone. [ 18 F]FDG PET/MRI showed a sensitivity of 61.7%, specificity of 84.9%, positive predictive value (PPV) of 49.2%, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 90.4% for multifocal disease detection. When combined with standard imaging, PPV increased to 63.6%; sensitivity was 29.8%. Conclusions [ 18 F]FDG PET/MRI substantially influences treatment decisions in EBC, modifying management in nearly one-third of patients. MRI was highly informative for detecting multifocal disease, whereas the potential added value of [ 18 F]FDG PET/MRI may primarily relate to integrated axillary and distant staging. However, its moderate diagnostic accuracy warrants caution to prevent overtreatment.

title: Gastrointestinal ultrasound in systemic sclerosis: A scoping review of current evidence.
abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease frequently associated with gastrointestinal (GI) involvement. GI manifestations are heterogeneous, may occur throughout the entire tract from the very early stages of the disease and are often associated with a significant burden of symptoms and complications, leading to high morbidity and mortality. Diagnosis often remains challenging due to the lack of sensitive instruments for early detection and the reliance on invasive or expensive diagnostic tools. In recent years, ultrasound (US) has become an increasingly important tool for GI evaluation across a wide range of conditions, including chronic inflammatory bowel diseases, appendicitis and diverticulitis as well as rarer diseases and functional conditions. The aim of this scoping review is to provide an updated overview of the role of gastrointestinal ultrasound (GIUS) in the assessment and monitoring of GI involvement in SSc. A systematic search of MEDLINE and Scopus identified 25 eligible studies. The available evidence is unevenly distributed across the GI tract: thirteen studies addressed the upper GI tract, seven the anorectum, six the gallbladder and five the mesenteric vessels. For each segment, we summarize how US can detect changes in wall structure, vascularization and motility. The evidence base is limited by small, predominantly single-center and cross-sectional studies, heterogeneous acquisition protocols and reference standards and a scarcity of reproducibility data. Further prospective and multicenter studies are therefore needed to validate the role of GIUS, standardize protocols and establish its integration into the clinical management of SSc patients.

title: Discovery of benzoxazole derivatives as novel α-synuclein aggregate ligands with potential for PET tracer development.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder worldwide, and the abnormal aggregation of α-synuclein (α-Syn) constitutes its core pathological hallmark. Positron emission tomography (PET) imaging of cerebral α-Syn aggregates holds great promise for the early diagnosis of PD. However, the imaging quality critically depends on the ligands with high binding affinity and selectivity for α-Syn aggregates. In this work, we developed a new type of benzoxazole-based α-Syn aggregate ligands via an SPR-based screening. Among them, candidates D15 (K D = 0.12 μM) and D16 (K D = 0.08 μM) exhibited high binding affinities for α-Syn aggregates in vitro and good potency in the SH-SY5Y cellular model and brain tissues from α-Syn PFF-injected PD mouse models, as well as excellent selectivity for tau and Aβ aggregates in rTg4510 and APP23 transgenic mouse brain sections. Thanks to their favorable blood-brain barrier permeability and suitable structures for radiolabeling for PET imaging, these new ligands represent promising candidates for the development of α-Syn PET radiotracers, offering a valuable foundation for the early diagnosis of PD and related synucleinopathies.

Thanks to their favorable blood-brain barrier permeability and suitable structures for radiolabeling for PET imaging, these new ligands represent promising candidates for the development of α-Syn PET radiotracers, offering a valuable foundation for the early diagnosis of PD and related synucleinopathies.

title: A liquid fiducial marker for image-guided proton beam therapy of abdominal tumors.
abstract: Purpose This study compared a liquid to solid fiducial markers regarding visibility, artifact characteristics on X-ray imaging and dose perturbation for image-guided proton therapy (IGPT) of abdominal tumors. Additionally, the radio-opaque composition of the liquid fiducial marker was optimized, and the chemical stability after proton beam irradiation was analyzed. Material and methods The fiducial markers inserted into an anthropomorphic abdominal phantom were exposed to X-ray, single-energy computed tomography (SECT), dual-energy CT (DECT) and cone-beam CT (CBCT) to determine contrast-to-noise ratios (CNR) and artifacts. Proton dose perturbation estimations were performed using a Monte Carlo dose algorithm. Chemical stability following proton beam irradiation was assessed with biophysical and optical methods. Results The CNR of the liquid marker with a volume ≥ 100 μl (CNR ≤ 2.69) on 2D X-ray images was superior to the solid markers (CNR ≤ 1.72). The artifact areas (A) and severity in the CT modalities were more pronounced for the solid (e.g. , sect A ≤ 279.4 mm 3 ) than for the liquid fiducial marker (A ≤ 30.5 mm 3 ). Dose mitigation of ≥ 50% in a proton beam was calculated for solid fiducial markers, while the liquid marker less influenced the dose distribution. Increasing radio-opaque content in the liquid prototypes improved visibility (CNR ≤ 2.97) without significantly increasing artifact volume (SECT: A ≤ 40.5 mm3) or dose perturbation. No degradation of the liquid fiducial marker's chemical composition was observed. Conclusion The liquid fiducial marker demonstrated comparable visibility and chemical stability with reduced artifact generation and dose perturbation compared to solid markers, indicating superiority for IGPT of abdominal tumors. Optimization of the liquid marker composition may be considered.

title: The medical physicist's role in the artificial intelligence era: an updated EFOMP curricular and professional framework.
abstract: Purpose Five years after the European Federation of Organizations for Medical Physics (EFOMP) published its first curricular framework for artificial intelligence (AI) in medical physics, the updated core curricula for radiology, radiotherapy and nuclear medicine have incorporated AI as a core competency rather than an addendum, a change consistent with the framework's principal recommendation. This paper examines the resulting educational landscape and defines the next stage of AI competency for the profession. Materials and methods Focus Group 3 of the EFOMP Artificial Intelligence Special Interest Group used a structured, iterative process of expert deliberation combining comparative curriculum analysis, competency mapping, regulatory analysis and iterative expert deliberation within the Working Group. Four primary source documents were analyzed in depth: the 2021 EFOMP white paper and the three updated EFOMP subspecialty core curricula for radiology, radiotherapy and nuclear medicine. The AI-related content of the three curricula was systematically compared against a predefined analytical framework covering scope, depth of treatment, European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System (ECTS) allocation, terminology, regulatory references, and treatment of recent AI developments. Competency gaps beyond the entry-level curricula were identified and articulated in the knowledge-skills-competence format used in EFOMP curricula. The resulting framework was informed by three large-scale surveys of medical physicists conducted in 2020, 2024 and 2025, and underwent iterative review within the Working Group before consultation within the EFOMP community. Results The three updated curricula converge on a shared methodological foundation but diverge in ECTS allocation, coverage of recent AI architectures, and treatment of the EU AI Act, and six competency gaps were identified as common to all three subspecialties. A cross-subspecialty advanced competency framework is proposed, organized into four domains: validation and quality assurance, AI lifecycle management, generative AI and foundation models, and governance. A professional lifecycle model is introduced describing how these competencies should be acquired during specialist training, maintained through accredited continuing professional development, and formally recognized throughout a medical physicist's career. The medical physicist's responsibilities under the EU AI Act are defined, and the proposed framework is translated into practical recommendations for EFOMP, its National Member Organizations, training centers, and individual practitioners. Conclusions The profession's challenge has evolved from demonstrating the importance of AI to ensuring its safe, trustworthy, effective and regulatory-compliant integration into clinical practice, thereby strengthening patient safety and quality of care.

title: Volume-based quantitative assessment of respiratory-induced organ motion in lung cancers.
abstract: Purpose To comprehensively evaluate respiratory-induced organ motion and deformation using volume-based analysis, overcoming the limitations of conventional point-based methods in radiation therapy for lung malignancies. Material and methods The Internal target volume (ITV) and organs at risk (OARs) were delineated on averaged-phase images from 4D-CT datasets of 11 lung cancer patients. Deformable image registration using an enhanced non-parametric algorithm generated deformation vector fields (DVFs) between each respiratory phase and a reference phase. Voxel-level displacements within each structure were statistically analyzed, quantifying ITV and OAR motion via geometric centroid displacement, mean voxel displacement, and 80th/90th percentile displacements. Pearson correlation analysis assessed the relationship between ITV motion and volumetric deformation, while one-way repeated-measures ANOVA evaluated directional consistency of OAR centroid and voxel-average displacements across LR, AP, and SI axes (p ≤0.05). Results Superior-inferior (SI) displacement of ITVs exceeded lateral and AP motion by 2-6 times. Significant centroid-voxel average motion discrepancies in the left lower lobe, right upper lobe, and diaphragm (p = 0.05) indicate limitations of point-based measures. The 80th percentile voxel motion showed potential as a centroid surrogate. Diaphragm and mediastinum deformation reached 60-80 %, with ITV deformation spanning 5-70 %. Motion metrics correlated strongly within structures but weakly with deformation. Conclusion This approach enables comprehensive quantification of respiratory motion, supporting optimized motion management in lung cancer radiotherapy. As conventional metrics fail to capture organ deformation, integrating both motion and deformation assessments is essential for accurately characterizing respiratory-induced target variations.

title: Asymptomatic congenital CMV infection: long-term cognitive outcome and brain imaging findings.
abstract: Background Infants with symptomatic congenital cytomegalovirus infection (cCMV) are at high risk of neurodevelopmental impairments. However, long-term cognitive outcomes in children with asymptomatic cCMV (acCMV) remain unclear. Patients and methods Through universal CMV screening of approximately 20,000 newborns, children with acCMV (n = 36), children with symptomatic cCMV (n = 4), and matched healthy controls (n = 54) were identified and followed prospectively. Brain MRI and neuropsychological assessments were performed in children with acCMV and controls at 6-8 years of age. Results Brain MRI findings were more common in children with acCMV than in controls (14/23, 60.9% vs. 3/31, 9.7%;p < 0.001). Punctate white matter lesions were the most frequent finding and occurred more often in children with acCMV than in controls (10/23, 43.5% vs. 3/31, 9.7%;p 0.004). Ventriculomegaly, cerebellar cortical malformations, and cerebral cortical malformations were less common and occurred only in children with acCMV. Mean full-scale IQ did not differ significantly between children with acCMV (n = 26) and controls (n = 28) (116.91 ± 11.67 vs. 118.68 ± 13.12, p NS), nor did the mean subtest scores. The full-scale IQ in children with acCMV with brain MRI abnormalities (n = 12) did not significantly differ from those without abnormalities (n = 8) (109.67 ± 13.72 vs. 120.75 ± 9.24, p NS). Neither did the mean subtest scores differ between them. Discussion Despite the high frequency of brain MRI abnormalities, predominantly white matter lesions, cognitive outcomes at early school-age did not differ significantly between children with acCMV and controls. Larger studies are needed to confirm these findings and determine the prognostic significance of brain MRI abnormalities in acCMV.

title: Radiolabelled cyclodextrins to detect cervical cancer: a preclinical feasibility study.
abstract: Radiolabelled cyclodextrins targeting prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) seem promising candidates for positron emission tomography (PET)-based molecular imaging of cervical cancer. Here, we evaluated the performance of gallium-68-labelled 2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HPβCD) and randomly methylated β-cyclodextrin (RAMEB) for the in vivo PET detection of cervical cancer. P-glycoprotein positive (Pgp+) KB-V-1 and P-glycoprotein negative (Pgp-) KB-3-1 cervical carcinoma xenografts of varying sizes (small-, medium-, large-sized) were established and subjected to [ 68 Ga]Ga-NODAGA-HPβCD and [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTAGA-RAMEB PET imaging followed by ex vivo biodistribution and immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis of PGE2 and Pgp expression. In line with the IHC results, PET data revealed the capability of both radiotracers to reliably detect each tumor types independent of tumor size. Nevertheless, the modest increase in uptake observed with increasing size may indicate enhanced tumor aggressiveness and angiogenic activity. Comparable radiotracer accumulation in MDR-positive and MDR-negative tumors suggests that HPβCD and RAMEB derivatives are unlikely to serve as substrates of Pgp enabling tumor detection across different tumor types. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that radiolabelled cyclodextrins are promising PET tracers for the in vivo detection of cervical cancer, irrespective of tumor size and Pgp expression.

title: Deep learning super-resolution enhances MRI radiomics for predicting placenta accreta spectrum and invasiveness.
abstract: Objectives Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) is a severe obstetric complication. This study evaluated whether retrospective, post-processing deep learning-based super-resolution reconstruction (SR) was associated with improved MRI radiomics performance for predicting PAS and invasive PAS. Materials & methods This retrospective study involved 245 patients who had placental MRI scans at three different institutions. Of these, 158 cases from Institution I for training set and internal validation set, while 34 patients from Institution II and 53 patients from Institution III served as external validation sets. SR using a generative adversarial network (GAN) was applied to generate SR T2WI (SRT2WI). Predictive models for PAS and invasive PAS were developed based on T2WI, SRT2WI, and the SRT2WI-Clinical model. Two radiologists independently diagnosed PAS using T2WI to serve as a reference for evaluating model performance. Model performance was assessed using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), Delong test, and net reclassification improvement (NRI). SHAP values interpreted the models and quantified feature contributions. Results Across all four cohorts, SRT2WI yielded numerically higher AUCs than T2WI, and SRT2WI-Clinical achieved the highest AUCs. For PAS, SRT2WI-Clinical achieved AUCs of 0.953, 0.887, 0.793, and 0.788 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts 1 and 2, respectively (T2WI: 0.738, 0.697, 0.654, and 0.652; SRT2WI: 0.879, 0.820, 0.696, and 0.768). Corresponding AUCs for invasive PAS were 0.895, 0.875, 0.843, and 0.815 (T2WI: 0.774, 0.699, 0.575, and 0.745; SRT2WI: 0.861, 0.794, 0.729, and 0.808). For PAS, SRT2WI-Clinical significantly outperformed T2WI (P < 0.001) and SRT2WI (P = 0.004) only in training, with no significant validation differences. For invasive PAS, it significantly outperformed T2WI in training, internal validation, and external validation cohort 1 (P = 0.003, 0.021, and 0.019, respectively), but not external validation cohort 2 (P = 0.398); comparisons with SRT2WI were nonsignificant. Calibration showed good agreement, DCA favored SRT2WI-Clinical, and SHAP quantified feature contributions. Conclusions The combination of SR and radiomics shows promise for improving the prediction of PAS and invasive PAS. Integrating clinical features may further enhance model performance, supporting its potential clinical utility.
